text: A researcher wants a fast estimate of protein-ligand binding free energy directly from an existing MD trajectory, and is willing to accept errors of roughly 2 to 5 kcal/mol. Which method should they use?
choices: Free Energy Perturbation (FEP) with multiple lambda-window simulations
Steered MD combined with the Jarzynski equality
Replica Exchange MD across a temperature ladder
MM-PBSA or MM-GBSA post-processing of the existing trajectory
explanation: MM-PBSA/MM-GBSA are post-processing methods that estimate binding free energy directly from existing trajectory frames (combining MM energy, implicit solvation, and an entropy estimate), trading accuracy for speed with typical errors of about 2 to 5 kcal/mol. FEP is more accurate (about 1 kcal/mol error) but requires many new simulations of non-physical intermediate states rather than reusing one trajectory, while REMD and steered MD/Jarzynski address enhanced sampling and pulling-based free energy profiles, not quick post-hoc binding estimates from a single trajectory.
